transcript:
Header: Redwood All-Hands - Nov 17, 2026
Date/Time: 2026-11-17 10:00 PT
Duration: ~64 minutes
Attendees: Alex, Sofia, Daniel, Priya, Ethan, Mina, Jordan + all employees (zoom)

[00:00] Alex Morgan: hey everyone, good morning, welcome to the November all-hands, um quick housekeeping, recording is on, we'll go about 60ish minutes and then drop into breakouts for team-level Q&A.

[00:23] Alex Morgan: Quick shoutout first, Q4 usage is trending ahead of plan, we saw a 28% month-over-month increase in token throughput across hosted accounts and a number of mid-market customers moved to Dedicated this month. so big thanks to product and sales.

[00:47] Sofia Lopez: yeah, and on the revenue side we closed three mid-market renewals with expansion add-ons, that helped with the monthly committed revenue bump. not to handwave but it's a mix of usage growth and a couple of larger expansion deals.

[01:10] Ethan Liu: one note - churn is holding stable, net revenue retention is 116% this quarter, helped by the new upsell bundles for the Console and Optimize feature. we still have room to improve in the retail vertical, but overall good momentum.

[01:36] Alex Morgan: okay product update, Priya?

[01:40] Priya Patel: cool, thanks. quick roadmap bullets - Dedicated GA improvements: we've shipped autoscaling policies for reserved pools, customers can now set burst capacity windows which has cut tail latency by about 12% in our internal tests. we also finished the first pass of the Dedicated pricing page, needs one more pass with GTM.

[02:04] Priya Patel: Private - several customers are in onboarding for VPC private deployments, a handful requested on-prem packaging for regulated workloads. Mina's team has been working with infra to support on-prem cert rotations and HSM integrations. small note, there's been some confusion in docs around KV cash metrics - sorry kv cash, that should be KV cache, we'll fix wording in docs.

[02:32] Mina Shah: yep, and from a research perspective we've got a new quantization profile for small sequence lengths that reduces GPU memory by ~30% with minor quality tradeoffs, this is in Optimize as a suggested profile. early customers are seeing cost wins.

[02:56] Daniel Park: on the runtime side we're rolling out a kernel selection change that picks different GEMM kernels based on seq len distribution. initial A/B shows 8-10% throughput improvements for long-context workloads. also added more observability for KV cache hit rates in the Console, Priya mentioned that.

[03:22] Alex Morgan: great, thank you. Operational review - Mina? you want to walk folks through the incident last week?

[03:28] Mina Shah: sure. So on Tuesday at ~03:15 UTC we had a degraded throughput event in one of the Dedicated clusters in eu-west. cause was a regression in our batching path plus a bad kernel selection fallback under memory pressure. the mitigation work took about 90 minutes to roll out a hotfix. postmortem's in draft - main takeaways: need better canarying for kernel selector changes, add a circuit breaker on batch sizes when memory pressure spikes, and improve the rollback automation.

[03:58] Mina Shah: I want to be clear - no customer data exposure, it was a perf/regression issue. I'm publishing the full postmortem by Monday, and we'll include proposed changes to our deployment pipeline.

[04:18] Alex Morgan: thanks Mina. any questions on that?

[04:23] [Silence / reactions]

[04:30] Sofia Lopez: ops ask - make sure SEs and support have a short FAQ to explain incident to customers, especially Dedicated customers who saw impact. Mina can you coordinate with support?

[04:40] Mina Shah: yes, I'll sync with Daniel and support, will produce a short customer-facing FAQ by Friday.

[04:48] Priya Patel: moving on to Console & Optimize - we've shipped token-level cost breakdowns to a pilot group, early feedback is that it's super helpful for chargebacks and engineering ownership, there's a small UX polish to do. Optimize is recommending batching profiles per route now, and one pilot cut unit cost by 22%.

[05:12] Daniel Park: technical note - the batching suggestions rely on request distribution snapshots, that means we need a low-overhead telemetry path. we prototyped an approach that samples prefix distributions and it looks promising, but we need to scale it.

[05:30] Alex Morgan: ok, hiring and org - Jordan?

[05:33] Jordan Reyes: headcount update - we're at ~148 folks, hiring plan for Q1 is ~25 roles prioritized on infra, SE, and product. we're accelerating internships for next summer and we're launching a referral sprint. offsite: start thinking about 2027 offsite - sending a short survey after this all-hands.

[05:52] Alex Morgan: finance / runway - Sofia?

[05:55] Sofia Lopez: runway is healthy post-Series C, burn is in line with plan, we have a small reforecast for Q4 given faster sales cycles. nothing alarming, but we'll share the board deck next week.

[06:10] Alex Morgan: quick competitive note - we're seeing faster experimentation from Anthropic and OpenAI on model features, and Hugging Face continues to push tooling for self-hosting. our edge is the combined runtime + product experience for serving and the cost/perf tooling. keep messaging that in customer decks.

[06:34] Priya Patel: customer feedback loop - we've opened a public roadmap board for prioritized features and customers can request access; also doing monthly product office hours with key customers.

[06:46] Ethan Liu: GTM - we're piloting a new expansion motion for existing customers: targeted audits using Console data, then a proposal that bundles Dedicated commitments with Optimize tuning. Early pilot showed a 17% ARR uplift for two accounts.

[07:04] Alex Morgan: ok questions from the queue - first is on Private/on-prem packaging and compliance.

[07:09] Mina Shah: yes, security update - SOC 2 Type II in final audit, ISO is in progress, and for customers wanting on-prem we now have a checklist for audit ops including KMS/HSM integration notes and recommended network diagrams. SEs will get the checklist.

[07:32] [Question] Employee: Can we get more clarity on Dedicated burst pricing?

[07:36] Priya Patel: short answer - burst windows are charged at a premium over reserved throughput, and there's an opt-in policy per pool. we're finishing exact numbers with finance, Priya to send final pricing next week.

[07:55] [Laughter]

[07:58] [Question] Employee: what's the plan for supporting longer context models?

[08:02] Daniel Park: longer context improvements are twofold - runtime batching and kernel selection for long sequences plus kv cache and prefix caching improvements. we're testing a memory-optimized path for 64k contexts but it's early. expect experimental support in Q2 2027.

[08:25] Alex Morgan: thank you. another question - will we expand to APAC cloud regions next year?

[08:29] Sofia Lopez: yes, regional expansion is in plan for H1 2027, partnering with cloud providers and channel partners. customers in APAC have asked for lower latency and local residency.

[08:43] [Question] Employee: how do we balance hosted vs private for enterprise pipeline?

[08:47] Ethan Liu: our playbook is to start customers on hosted for fast time-to-value, move to Dedicated for committed capacity and predictability, and Private/on-prem for regulated customers. the Console and rollout policies make that transition easier.

[09:05] Alex Morgan: Cool, closing remarks - recap of key priorities: 1) reliability work and postmortem follow-through, 2) finalize Dedicated pricing and GTM materials, 3) ship Console telemetry and KV cache dashboards, 4) hiring for infra and SEs.

[09:27] Alex Morgan: Thanks team, reminders - watch for the postmortem, Priya's pricing doc, and Jordan's offsite survey. We'll break into team-level rooms in about five, leadership will stick around for a short ask-and-answer.

[09:39] [End of main all-hands, transition to breakouts]

Notes: transcript contains occasional transcription errors (e.g., "KV cash" instead of KV cache), filler words and overlapping speech. References to decks and docs: "Q4 board deck" (to be shared), "Dedicated pricing page" (link to be posted in Slack), "incident postmortem" (will be posted in Confluence).
